title: The sinoatrial node sets the usual rhythm of the heart
summary: OpenStax says the sinoatrial node is the pacemaker because it has the highest built-in rate and starts the usual rhythm.
body: OpenStax says heart muscle can start an electrical potential at a fixed rate that spreads from cell to cell. It calls that property autorhythmicity, and it says neither nor skeletal muscle can do it. The sinoatrial node, a clump of cells in the right atrium, has the highest built-in rate and is called the pacemaker. It starts the sinus rhythm. Without nervous or hormone control, the text says that node would start about 80 to 100 times a minute. Those systems do change the rate. This card names the pacemaker. It is not a device implanted by a surgeon.
